chunks: With the first chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Amru ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon them both, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, was among you in Kufa. He used to set out early every day from his residence, touring the markets of Kufa one by one, with a whip on his shoulder that had two sharp ends and was called al-Sabibah.

He said: He would stand in each market and call out: "O company of merchants! Seek divine guidance, and seek blessing through easy dealings. Draw near to the buyers and adorn yourselves with forbearance. Refrain from oaths and avoid lying. Abstain from injustice and be fair to the oppressed. Do not approach usury. Give full measure and weight, and do not diminish for people their things, and do not act corruptly on earth as corrupters."

He said: Thus he would tour all the markets of Kufa, then return and sit to attend to the people. He said: When they saw him approaching and he called: "O people!", they would stop their dealings, listen to him attentively with their ears, and gaze upon him with their eyes until he, peace be upon him, finished his speech. When he finished, they would say: "We hear and we obey, O Commander of the Faithful."
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali supervise the markets of Kufa?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir narrates how Imam Ali, during his caliphate in Kufa, would personally tour the marketplace each morning carrying a whip called al-Sabibah, delivering ethical instructions to merchants. His commands — seeking divine guidance, treating buyers gently, avoiding false oaths, lying, injustice, usury, and unfair measures — echo Quranic injunctions on fair commerce. The people of Kufa responded with complete obedience and respect.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 31. With the first chain of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Amru ibn Abi al-Miqdam (from Jabir), from: Abu Ja’far, Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon them both, who said:

‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, was among you in Kufa and he used to come out early in the morning from his residence, visiting each market of Kufa, one after another, with a whip on his shoulder. It had two sharp ends and was thus called al-Sabibah.

He said: He (i.e. ‘Ali) would stand in every market and say: "O business people! Seek providence of Allah and earn His bounty by easy trade! Endear yourselves to the buyers and adorn yourselves with patience. And do not swear or take oath; refrain from lies and do not associate with inequity. Come to the rescue of the wronged ones by obtaining justice for them, and do not deal in usury. Give full measure and weight and do not diminish for people their things, and do not work corruption on the earth."

He said: Thus he (i.e. ‘Ali) toured all the markets of Kufa and then returned to his place for listening to the common people. He said: When the market people saw him approaching them, exclaiming: "O People!, they would stop their dealings, listen to him carefully and regard him respectfully till he finished." Then they would respond: "With all readiness, we obey you O, Amirul Mu’mineen."
